newsitem.title: USA: Clinton backs grassroots campaign fund reform bid.
newsitem.headline: Clinton backs grassroots campaign fund reform bid.

text.p: President Clinton encouraged Americans on Wednesday to sign a petition calling for campaign finance reform, saying this grassroots effort could "help break the logjam" in tempering the power of money in politics.

"Passage of effective campaign finance reform must be a priority for this Congress, but we will succeed only if citizens all across the country make clear to elected officials that change is urgent, and that public support is broad and deep," Clinton said in a statement.

The Democratic president specifically endorsed "Project Independence," a drive by Common Cause, a campaign watchdog group, and Campaign For America, a civic action group founded by financier Jerome Kohlberg, to collect 1,776,000 signatures of support for campaign finance reform.
"Project Independence can help break the logjam that has blocked reform for so long," he said.

The groups back a campaign finance reform bill sponsored by Arizona Republican Sen. John McCain and Wisconsin Democratic Sen. Russell Feingold that bans large corporate and labour "soft money" donations to parties and puts voluntary limits on spending, among other things.

Clinton, whose own 1996 re-election campaign fundraising tactics have sparked intense controversy and triggered several congressional investigation, also backs the McCain-Feingold bill and called for its passage by U.S. Independence Day on July 4.
